'''SoapBox Law''' is the public-legal-record vertical of the [[SoapBox]] ecosystem, published at law.soapbox.community. It presents U.S. caselaw, statutes, regulations, judges and lawyer records — facts from the public reporters, source-linked, keyless and free — alongside a set of plain-English explainer pages on how the law is actually structured.

The stated editorial rule is ''facts, not verdicts'': a case description says what a decision is cited for as a matter of legal-historical record, not whether the site thinks the decision is correct. Everything is informational, not legal advice.

== The record ==
* '''Cases''' — searchable opinions from the public reporters, each linked to its source of record.
* '''Statutes & Code''' and '''Regulations''' — the statutory and regulatory layers.
* '''Judges''' and '''Lawyers''' — public records on the people in the system.
* '''File a complaint''' — a routing page to legal aid, bar referral, and consumer/fraud complaint channels.

== The explainer pages ==
These are short, cited guides to how U.S. law fits together. Each is its own article here:
* [[Privacy Law]] — federal (sectoral) privacy law and where Texas replaces, adds to or limits it.
* [[Rights That Hold Up in Court]] — which rights are real and which are pseudolegal folklore, with the actual cases.
* [[Foundational Law]] — the Constitution: three branches, four layers, and how they check each other.
* [[Treaties]] — how a treaty is made and when it becomes enforceable law inside the United States.
* [[Legal Maxims]] — legal maxims, political axioms and idioms, each with a gloss and a source.
